_comment: Tier-2 for skfem hyperelasticity#3, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: F = I + grad(u); dropping the identity makes F = 0 at the reference configuration, det(F) = 0, lnJ = -inf, and the first residual out of asm is NaN or wildly too large. Ran: MeshTri().refined(3), ElementVector(ElementTriP1), 162 DOFs, mu=lam=1, both kernels assembled at u = 0 under warnings.catch_warnings(record=True), then three Newton steps each toward a 5% right-edge stretch. Printed: with the identity F[0,0] = 1, det(F) = 1 everywhere and the first residual is exactly 0.000e+00; without it F[0,0] = 0, det(F) = 0 everywhere and the residual is NaN in every entry -- the NaN branch of the claim, not the too-large branch. The ONLY thing emitted is one numpy RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in divide' from skfem.helpers.inv; nothing raises and the Newton loop completes. NEW: the resulting displacement is NaN on every FREE DOF but finite on the constrained ones because condense writes the prescribed values in verbatim, so a check of np.isnan(u).all() misses it while isfinite(u).all() catches it.
